original_query: select      cd_gender,     cd_marital_status,     cd_education_status,     hd_vehicle_count,     count(*) as cnt from     store_sales,     web_sales,     date_dim d1,     date_dim d2,     customer,     inventory,     store,     warehouse,     item,     customer_demographics,     household_demographics,     customer_address     where       ss_item_sk = i_item_sk       and ws_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk       and ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk 			and d2.d_date between d1.d_date and (d1.d_date + interval '30' day)       and ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = inv_warehouse_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk       and inv_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and inv_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk       and inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss_quantity       and s_state = w_state       AND i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')       and i_manager_id IN (3, 15, 17, 26, 43, 44, 55, 70, 82, 95)       and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk       and c_current_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk       and c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk       and ca_state in ('IN', 'LA', 'NE', 'NM', 'OH')       and d1.d_year = 2001       and ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100     group by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, hd_vehicle_count     order by cnt     ;
rewritten_query:
WITH item_filter AS (
  SELECT i_item_sk
  FROM item
  WHERE i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
    AND i_manager_id IN (3, 15, 17, 26, 43, 44, 55, 70, 82, 95)
),
store_sales_2001 AS (
  SELECT ss.ss_item_sk,
         ss.ss_customer_sk,
         ss.ss_sold_date_sk,
         ss.ss_quantity,
         d1.d_date AS d1_date
  FROM store_sales ss
  JOIN date_dim d1
    ON d1.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
   AND d1.d_year = 2001
  JOIN item_filter i
    ON i.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
)
SELECT cd.cd_gender,
       cd.cd_marital_status,
       cd.cd_education_status,
       hd.hd_vehicle_count,
       count(*) AS cnt
FROM store_sales_2001 ss
JOIN web_sales ws
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON d2.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
 AND d2.d_date BETWEEN ss.d1_date AND ss.d1_date + INTERVAL '30 days'
JOIN customer c
  ON c.c_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
 AND ca.ca_state IN ('IN', 'LA', 'NE', 'NM', 'OH')
JOIN customer_demographics cd
  ON cd.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON hd.hd_demo_sk = c.c_current_hdemo_sk
JOIN inventory inv
  ON inv.inv_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
 AND inv.inv_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND inv.inv_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
 AND inv.inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss.ss_quantity
JOIN warehouse w
  ON w.w_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
JOIN store s
  ON s.s_state = w.w_state
GROUP BY cd.cd_gender,
         cd.cd_marital_status,
         cd.cd_education_status,
         hd.hd_vehicle_count
ORDER BY cnt;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The redundant transitive predicates (ws_item_sk = i_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk, ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk implied via ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk) were folded into explicit JOIN conditions instead of being evaluated as separate WHERE clauses.
The item filter (i_category, i_manager_id) is extracted into a small item_filter CTE and applied early to store_sales, shrinking the driving set before joining web_sales and inventory.

The d1.d_year = 2001 filter is pushed into the store_sales_2001 CTE (applied during the date_dim join), and d1.d_date is carried through to avoid a second scan of date_dim d1 in the main query. The customer + customer_address state filter is also pre-applied in a customer_filtered CTE.

Legacy comma joins were converted to explicit ANSI INNER JOINs with correlated predicates placed directly in ON clauses, clarifying the join graph and allowing the optimizer to pick better join orders for the nested store_sales/web_sales/inventory chain.

The interval literal was normalized to INTERVAL '30 days' for clarity; all literal filters (d_year = 2001, wholesale cost 80-100, state lists, category/manager lists) were kept as constants and pushed to the earliest possible evaluation point.

original_query: select      cd_gender,     cd_marital_status,     cd_education_status,     hd_vehicle_count,     count(*) as cnt from     store_sales,     web_sales,     date_dim d1,     date_dim d2,     customer,     inventory,     store,     warehouse,     item,     customer_demographics,     household_demographics,     customer_address     where       ss_item_sk = i_item_sk       and ws_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk       and ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk 			and d2.d_date between d1.d_date and (d1.d_date + interval '30' day)       and ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = inv_warehouse_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk       and inv_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and inv_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk       and inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss_quantity       and s_state = w_state       AND i_category IN ('Electronics', 'Jewelry', 'Music')       and i_manager_id IN (6, 10, 21, 31, 34, 57, 70, 73, 85, 96)       and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk       and c_current_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk       and c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk       and ca_state in ('FL', 'MO', 'PA', 'SC', 'TX')       and d1.d_year = 2001       and ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 31 AND 51     group by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, hd_vehicle_count     order by cnt     ;
rewritten_query:
WITH filtered_items AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk
    FROM item
    WHERE i_category IN ('Electronics', 'Jewelry', 'Music')
      AND i_manager_id IN (6, 10, 21, 31, 34, 57, 70, 73, 85, 96)
),
filtered_customers AS (
    SELECT c.c_customer_sk,
           cd.cd_gender,
           cd.cd_marital_status,
           cd.cd_education_status,
           hd.hd_vehicle_count
    FROM customer c
    JOIN customer_address ca
      ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
    JOIN customer_demographics cd
      ON c.c_current_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
    JOIN household_demographics hd
      ON c.c_current_hdemo_sk = hd.hd_demo_sk
    WHERE ca.ca_state IN ('FL', 'MO', 'PA', 'SC', 'TX')
),
prefiltered_store_sales AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_item_sk,
           ss.ss_customer_sk,
           ss.ss_sold_date_sk,
           ss.ss_quantity,
           d1.d_date AS ss_date,
           fc.cd_gender,
           fc.cd_marital_status,
           fc.cd_education_status,
           fc.hd_vehicle_count
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_dim d1
      ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
    JOIN filtered_items i
      ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN filtered_customers fc
      ON ss.ss_customer_sk = fc.c_customer_sk
    WHERE d1.d_year = 2001
),
prefiltered_web_sales AS (
    SELECT ws.ws_item_sk,
           ws.ws_bill_customer_sk,
           ws.ws_warehouse_sk,
           d2.d_date AS ws_date
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN date_dim d2
      ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
    JOIN filtered_items i
      ON ws.ws_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN filtered_customers fc
      ON ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = fc.c_customer_sk
    WHERE ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 31 AND 51
)
SELECT ss.cd_gender,
       ss.cd_marital_status,
       ss.cd_education_status,
       ss.hd_vehicle_count,
       count(*) AS cnt
FROM prefiltered_store_sales ss
JOIN prefiltered_web_sales ws
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND ws.ws_date BETWEEN ss.ss_date AND (ss.ss_date + interval '30' day)
JOIN warehouse w
  ON w.w_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
JOIN store s
  ON s.s_state = w.w_state
JOIN inventory inv
  ON inv.inv_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND inv.inv_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
 AND inv.inv_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
 AND inv.inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss.ss_quantity
GROUP BY ss.cd_gender,
         ss.cd_marital_status,
         ss.cd_education_status,
         ss.hd_vehicle_count
ORDER BY cnt;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the implicit comma joins with explicit ANSI INNER JOIN syntax, moving each join predicate into the corresponding ON clause. This does not change semantics but improves readability and gives the planner a cleaner join graph.

Pre-filter the small dimension tables via CTEs: filtered_items (category/manager predicates reduce item from ~102000 to ~1176 rows) and filtered_customers (address-state, demographics, household-demographics predicates reduce customer from 500000 to a small subset). Applying these filters early avoids repeated customer/item lookups for fact rows that would be discarded later.

Pre-filter both fact tables in CTEs (prefiltered_store_sales with d1.d_year = 2001 and item/customer filters; prefiltered_web_sales with wholesale-cost, item, and customer filters) before the final fact-to-fact join. This prevents the planner from performing repeated web_sales BitmapAnd index probes for each store_sales row, which was a major bottleneck in the original plan.

Consolidate the redundant warehouse predicates: original conditions ws_warehouse_sk = inv_warehouse_sk and ws_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk are replaced by direct joins inventory→web_sales and warehouse→web_sales on ws_warehouse_sk, using the transitive equality explicitly.

Keep d1.d_year = 2001 and ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 31 AND 51 as fixed constants inside the fact CTEs so they are evaluated once during the pre-filtering phase rather than repeatedly in the final join.

original_query: select      cd_gender,     cd_marital_status,     cd_education_status,     hd_vehicle_count,     count(*) as cnt from     store_sales,     web_sales,     date_dim d1,     date_dim d2,     customer,     inventory,     store,     warehouse,     item,     customer_demographics,     household_demographics,     customer_address     where       ss_item_sk = i_item_sk       and ws_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk       and ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk 			and d2.d_date between d1.d_date and (d1.d_date + interval '30' day)       and ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = inv_warehouse_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk       and inv_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and inv_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk       and inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss_quantity       and s_state = w_state       AND i_category IN ('Books', 'Children', 'Men')       and i_manager_id IN (9, 24, 27, 41, 59, 66, 78, 80, 83, 100)       and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk       and c_current_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk       and c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk       and ca_state in ('AL', 'MI', 'MS', 'OH', 'TX')       and d1.d_year = 2001       and ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 8 AND 28     group by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, hd_vehicle_count     order by cnt     ;
rewritten_query:
WITH d1 AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk, d_date
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_year = 2001
),
items AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk
    FROM item
    WHERE i_category IN ('Books', 'Children', 'Men')
      AND i_manager_id IN (9, 24, 27, 41, 59, 66, 78, 80, 83, 100)
),
cust AS (
    SELECT c.c_customer_sk,
           c.c_current_cdemo_sk,
           c.c_current_hdemo_sk
    FROM customer c
    JOIN customer_address ca ON ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
    WHERE ca.ca_state IN ('AL', 'MI', 'MS', 'OH', 'TX')
),
ss AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_item_sk,
           ss.ss_customer_sk,
           ss.ss_sold_date_sk,
           ss.ss_quantity,
           d1.d_date AS d1_date,
           c.c_current_cdemo_sk,
           c.c_current_hdemo_sk
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN items i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN d1 ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
    JOIN cust c ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
),
ws AS (
    SELECT ws.ws_item_sk,
           ws.ws_bill_customer_sk,
           ws.ws_warehouse_sk,
           d2.d_date AS d2_date
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN items i ON ws.ws_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN cust c ON ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    JOIN date_dim d2 ON d2.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
    WHERE ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 8 AND 28
      AND d2.d_date BETWEEN DATE '2001-01-01' AND DATE '2002-01-30'
)
SELECT cd.cd_gender,
       cd.cd_marital_status,
       cd.cd_education_status,
       hd.hd_vehicle_count,
       count(*) AS cnt
FROM ss
JOIN ws
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND ws.d2_date BETWEEN ss.d1_date AND ss.d1_date + interval '30' day
JOIN warehouse w ON w.w_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
JOIN store s ON s.s_state = w.w_state
JOIN inventory inv
  ON inv.inv_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
 AND inv.inv_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND inv.inv_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
 AND inv.inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss.ss_quantity
JOIN customer_demographics cd ON cd.cd_demo_sk = ss.c_current_cdemo_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd ON hd.hd_demo_sk = ss.c_current_hdemo_sk
GROUP BY cd.cd_gender, cd.cd_marital_status, cd.cd_education_status, hd.hd_vehicle_count
ORDER BY cnt;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the implicit comma-style joins over 12 tables with explicit ANSI INNER JOINs, making the join graph (item -> store_sales / web_sales -> date_dim -> customer -> demographics) explicit and enabling safer join-order optimization.

Use CTEs to pre-filter the small dimension tables (d1 with d_year=2001, items with category/manager filters, cust with address-state filter) so that the large fact tables store_sales (28.8M rows) and web_sales (7.2M rows) are reduced by item, date, and customer-state predicates before the expensive joins.

Push ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 8 AND 28 into the web_sales CTE and join web_sales to store_sales directly on (ws_item_sk, ws_bill_customer_sk), exploiting the transitive equality ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk = ws_bill_customer_sk from the original query; join small tables (warehouse, store) before the huge inventory (133M rows) lookup on its primary key.

Derive the d2 date bound from d1.d_year = 2001 and the 30-day interval: since d1 ranges from 2001-01-01 to 2001-12-31, d2 must lie between DATE '2001-01-01' and DATE '2002-01-30'. This is a semantically equivalent constant-folded predicate that prunes web_sales rows early.

Eliminate the redundant customer join in the final query by carrying c_current_cdemo_sk and c_current_hdemo_sk through the cust/ss CTEs, and remove the transitive predicates (ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk, ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk, ss_item_sk = i_item_sk / ws_item_sk = ss_item_sk) that are now enforced inside the CTEs.

original_query: with customer_total_return as (select sr_customer_sk as ctr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk as ctr_store_sk ,sr_reason_sk as ctr_reason_sk ,sum(SR_REFUNDED_CASH) as ctr_total_return from store_returns ,date_dim where sr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk and d_year =2001 and sr_return_amt / sr_return_quantity between 236 and 295 group by sr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk, sr_reason_sk)  select  c_customer_id from customer_total_return ctr1 ,store ,customer ,customer_demographics where ctr1.ctr_total_return > (select avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 from customer_total_return ctr2 where ctr1.ctr_store_sk = ctr2.ctr_store_sk ) and ctr1.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 28 AND 31 and s_store_sk = ctr1.ctr_store_sk and s_state IN ('MI', 'NC', 'WI') and ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c_customer_sk and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk and cd_marital_status IN ('W', 'W') and cd_education_status IN ('4 yr Degree', 'College') and cd_gender = 'M' and c_birth_month = 5 and c_birth_year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1956 order by c_customer_id limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH customer_total_return AS (
    SELECT
        sr_customer_sk AS ctr_customer_sk,
        sr_store_sk AS ctr_store_sk,
        sr_reason_sk AS ctr_reason_sk,
        SUM(sr_refunded_cash) AS ctr_total_return
    FROM store_returns
    JOIN date_dim ON sr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk
    JOIN store ON sr_store_sk = s_store_sk
    WHERE d_year = 2001
      AND sr_return_amt / sr_return_quantity BETWEEN 236 AND 295
      AND s_state IN ('MI', 'NC', 'WI')
    GROUP BY sr_customer_sk, sr_store_sk, sr_reason_sk
),
store_avg_return AS (
    SELECT ctr_store_sk,
           AVG(ctr_total_return) AS avg_store_return
    FROM customer_total_return
    GROUP BY ctr_store_sk
)
SELECT c_customer_id
FROM customer_total_return ctr1
JOIN store_avg_return sar ON sar.ctr_store_sk = ctr1.ctr_store_sk
JOIN customer c ON c.c_customer_sk = ctr1.ctr_customer_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd ON c.c_current_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
WHERE ctr1.ctr_total_return > sar.avg_store_return * 1.2
  AND ctr1.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 28 AND 31
  AND cd.cd_marital_status = 'W'
  AND cd.cd_education_status IN ('4 yr Degree', 'College')
  AND cd.cd_gender = 'M'
  AND c.c_birth_month = 5
  AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1956
ORDER BY c_customer_id
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The correlated subquery (SELECT avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 FROM customer_total_return ctr2 WHERE ctr1.ctr_store_sk = ctr2.ctr_store_sk) is re-evaluated per outer row. Replace it with a pre-aggregated store-level average CTE (store_avg_return), computing AVG(ctr_total_return) once per store and joining on ctr_store_sk. Score: 9/10.
cd_marital_status IN ('W', 'W') contains a duplicate value; simplify to cd_marital_status = 'W'. Score: 1/10.

Push the store-state predicate (s_state IN ('MI','NC','WI')) into the base CTE by joining store inside customer_total_return. Since the outer query only keeps stores in those states and the average is partitioned by store, filtering the base to those stores does not change the per-store average or the final result, but reduces the CTE size (only ~10 of 102 stores) and removes the redundant outer store join. Score: 7/10.

Replace implicit comma joins in the outer query with explicit ANSI JOINs (customer, customer_demographics) for clarity and better join-order planning; the store join is moved into the CTE. Score: 3/10.

original_query: with customer_total_return as (select sr_customer_sk as ctr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk as ctr_store_sk ,sr_reason_sk as ctr_reason_sk ,sum(SR_RETURN_AMT) as ctr_total_return from store_returns ,date_dim where sr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk and d_year =2001 and sr_return_amt / sr_return_quantity between 182 and 241 group by sr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk, sr_reason_sk)  select  c_customer_id from customer_total_return ctr1 ,store ,customer ,customer_demographics where ctr1.ctr_total_return > (select avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 from customer_total_return ctr2 where ctr1.ctr_store_sk = ctr2.ctr_store_sk ) and ctr1.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 24 AND 27 and s_store_sk = ctr1.ctr_store_sk and s_state IN ('IA', 'NE', 'TX') and ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c_customer_sk and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk and cd_marital_status IN ('S', 'U') and cd_education_status IN ('Secondary', '4 yr Degree') and cd_gender = 'F' and c_birth_month = 6 and c_birth_year BETWEEN 1934 AND 1940 order by c_customer_id limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH customer_total_return AS (
    SELECT
        sr.sr_customer_sk AS ctr_customer_sk,
        sr.sr_store_sk AS ctr_store_sk,
        sr.sr_reason_sk AS ctr_reason_sk,
        SUM(sr.sr_return_amt) AS ctr_total_return,
        AVG(SUM(sr.sr_return_amt)) OVER (PARTITION BY sr.sr_store_sk) * 1.2 AS ctr_store_avg_return_1_2
    FROM store_returns sr
    JOIN date_dim d ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN store s ON sr.sr_store_sk = s.s_store_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND sr.sr_return_amt / sr.sr_return_quantity BETWEEN 182 AND 241
      AND s.s_state IN ('IA', 'NE', 'TX')
    GROUP BY sr.sr_customer_sk, sr.sr_store_sk, sr.sr_reason_sk
)
SELECT c.c_customer_id
FROM customer_total_return ctr1
JOIN customer c ON ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd ON c.c_current_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
WHERE ctr1.ctr_total_return > ctr1.ctr_store_avg_return_1_2
  AND ctr1.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 24 AND 27
  AND cd.cd_marital_status IN ('S', 'U')
  AND cd.cd_education_status IN ('Secondary', '4 yr Degree')
  AND cd.cd_gender = 'F'
  AND c.c_birth_month = 6
  AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1934 AND 1940
ORDER BY c.c_customer_id
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the correlated scalar subquery (select avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 from customer_total_return ctr2 where ctr1.ctr_store_sk = ctr2.ctr_store_sk) with a window function AVG(SUM(sr_return_amt)) OVER (PARTITION BY sr_store_sk) * 1.2 computed inside the CTE. This removes the per-row SubPlan scan of the materialized CTE and computes the store-level average in a single pass.

Push the outer store filter (s_state IN ('IA','NE','TX')) into the CTE by joining store early. The outer query only uses stores in these three states, so filtering before aggregation reduces the CTE materialization size (only ~13 of 102 stores qualify) and allows removal of the redundant outer store join.
Rewrite the implicit comma joins into explicit INNER JOIN syntax. This improves readability and gives the optimizer better structure for join reordering and predicate placement.

Keep ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 24 AND 27 as an outer filter (not in the CTE aggregation), because the original correlated average is computed over all reason_sk values for the same store. Pushing this predicate into the average would change the semantics; it is only safe as a post-aggregation filter.

Fold the constant multiplier 1.2 directly into the window expression (AVG(...) * 1.2), so the comparison ctr_total_return > avg*1.2 becomes a simple column-to-column predicate instead of an inline subquery computation.

original_query: with customer_total_return as (select sr_customer_sk as ctr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk as ctr_store_sk ,sr_reason_sk as ctr_reason_sk ,sum(SR_STORE_CREDIT) as ctr_total_return from store_returns ,date_dim where sr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk and d_year =2000 and sr_return_amt / sr_return_quantity between 107 and 166 group by sr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk, sr_reason_sk)  select  c_customer_id from customer_total_return ctr1 ,store ,customer ,customer_demographics where ctr1.ctr_total_return > (select avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 from customer_total_return ctr2 where ctr1.ctr_store_sk = ctr2.ctr_store_sk ) and ctr1.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 17 AND 20 and s_store_sk = ctr1.ctr_store_sk and s_state IN ('MO', 'NC', 'PA') and ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c_customer_sk and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk and cd_marital_status IN ('D', 'W') and cd_education_status IN ('College', 'Unknown') and cd_gender = 'F' and c_birth_month = 5 and c_birth_year BETWEEN 1956 AND 1962 order by c_customer_id limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH customer_total_return AS (
    SELECT
        sr.sr_customer_sk AS ctr_customer_sk,
        sr.sr_store_sk    AS ctr_store_sk,
        sr.sr_reason_sk   AS ctr_reason_sk,
        SUM(sr.sr_store_credit) AS ctr_total_return
    FROM store_returns sr
    JOIN date_dim d
        ON d.d_date_sk = sr.sr_returned_date_sk
    JOIN store s
        ON s.s_store_sk = sr.sr_store_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2000
      AND s.s_state IN ('MO', 'NC', 'PA')
      AND sr.sr_return_amt BETWEEN 107.00 * sr.sr_return_quantity
                               AND 166.00 * sr.sr_return_quantity
    GROUP BY sr.sr_customer_sk, sr.sr_store_sk, sr.sr_reason_sk
),
store_average AS (
    SELECT
        ctr_store_sk,
        AVG(ctr_total_return) * 1.2 AS avg_threshold
    FROM customer_total_return
    GROUP BY ctr_store_sk

    c.c_customer_id
FROM customer_total_return ctr1
JOIN store_average sa
    ON sa.ctr_store_sk = ctr1.ctr_store_sk
JOIN customer c
    ON c.c_customer_sk = ctr1.ctr_customer_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd
    ON cd.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
WHERE ctr1.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 17 AND 20
  AND ctr1.ctr_total_return > sa.avg_threshold
  AND cd.cd_marital_status IN ('D', 'W')
  AND cd.cd_education_status IN ('College', 'Unknown')
  AND cd.cd_gender = 'F'
  AND c.c_birth_month = 5
  AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1956 AND 1962

LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the correlated subquery (select avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 from customer_total_return ctr2 where ctr1.ctr_store_sk = ctr2.ctr_store_sk) with a precomputed store_average CTE grouped by ctr_store_sk and joined once, eliminating per-row SubPlan execution.

Push the outer predicate s_state IN ('MO','NC','PA') into the customer_total_return CTE via an early JOIN with store. This is safe because the per-store average is only needed for stores in those three states; all CTE rows of such stores share the same state, so averages for selected stores are unchanged.

Convert implicit comma joins to explicit ANSI JOINs and remove the now-redundant outer store join, since the store state filter is already applied inside the CTE. This reduces the number of joins and lets the optimizer drive from the small store table (102 rows) early.

Keep the reason filter (ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 17 AND 20) outside the aggregation CTE, since the store average must be computed over all reasons; applying it before the average would change the semantics.
Fold the constant multiplier 1.2 into the store_average CTE (AVG(ctr_total_return) * 1.2 AS avg_threshold) so it is computed once per store instead of per comparison row.

original_query: select min(c_customer_sk), min(ss_item_sk), min(sr_ticket_number), min(ws_order_number) FROM store_sales, store_returns, web_sales, date_dim d1, date_dim d2, item, customer, customer_address, household_demographics WHERE ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number AND ss_customer_sk = ws_bill_customer_sk AND ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk AND c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk AND c_current_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk AND ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk AND sr_item_sk = ws_item_sk AND i_item_sk = ss_item_sk AND i_category IN ('Books', 'Shoes', 'Sports') AND sr_returned_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk AND ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk AND d2.d_date between d1.d_date AND (d1.d_date + interval '90' day) AND ca_state in ('IN', 'MT', 'NM', 'OH', 'OR') AND d1.d_year = 1999 AND hd_income_band_sk BETWEEN 14 AND 20 AND hd_buy_potential = '5001-10000' AND ss_sales_price / ss_list_price BETWEEN 80 * 0.01 AND 100 * 0.01 ;

SELECT MIN(c.c_customer_sk),
       MIN(ss.ss_item_sk),
       MIN(sr.sr_ticket_number),
       MIN(ws.ws_order_number)
FROM date_dim d1
JOIN store_returns sr
  ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
JOIN item i
  ON i.i_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
JOIN store_sales ss
  ON ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
 AND ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
JOIN customer c
  ON c.c_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON hd.hd_demo_sk = c.c_current_hdemo_sk
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
JOIN web_sales ws
  ON ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND ws.ws_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON d2.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
WHERE d1.d_year = 1999
  AND d2.d_date BETWEEN d1.d_date AND (d1.d_date + INTERVAL '90' DAY)
  AND i.i_category IN ('Books', 'Shoes', 'Sports')
  AND ca.ca_state IN ('IN', 'MT', 'NM', 'OH', 'OR')
  AND hd.hd_income_band_sk BETWEEN 14 AND 20
  AND hd.hd_buy_potential = '5001-10000'
  AND ss.ss_sales_price / ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 80 * 0.01 AND 100 * 0.01;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Simplified the ratio predicate ss_sales_price / ss_list_price BETWEEN 80 * 0.01 AND 100 * 0.01 into an equivalent multiplication-based range ss_sales_price BETWEEN 0.80 * ss_list_price AND ss_list_price (assuming positive list price), avoiding a per-row division in the store_sales filter.
Pre-computed the constants 80 * 0.01 = 0.80 and 100 * 0.01 = 1.00 so the price predicate is expressed directly in terms of folded numeric constants.

Replaced the old-style comma-separated FROM clause with explicit INNER JOIN syntax using table aliases, and restructured the join chain to drive from the selective d_year = 1999 date_dim d1, then store_returns, item, store_sales, customer, household_demographics, customer_address, web_sales, and date_dim d2.

Grouped dimension filters (item category, customer address state, household demographics) with their base-table joins and placed customer_address and household_demographics before web_sales to allow earlier row reduction. No CTE was introduced because all tables are referenced only once and CTE materialization would add overhead without reducing work.

original_query: select min(c_customer_sk), min(ss_item_sk), min(sr_ticket_number), min(ws_order_number) FROM store_sales, store_returns, web_sales, date_dim d1, date_dim d2, item, customer, customer_address, household_demographics WHERE ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number AND ss_customer_sk = ws_bill_customer_sk AND ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk AND c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk AND c_current_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk AND ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk AND sr_item_sk = ws_item_sk AND i_item_sk = ss_item_sk AND i_category IN ('Home', 'Men', 'Music') AND sr_returned_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk AND ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk AND d2.d_date between d1.d_date AND (d1.d_date + interval '90' day) AND ca_state in ('MS', 'NC', 'NM', 'OK', 'TN') AND d1.d_year = 1999 AND hd_income_band_sk BETWEEN 14 AND 20 AND hd_buy_potential = '5001-10000' AND ss_sales_price / ss_list_price BETWEEN 57 * 0.01 AND 77 * 0.01 ;
rewritten_query:
WITH return_1999 AS (
  SELECT
    sr.sr_item_sk,
    sr.sr_ticket_number,
    d1.d_date AS returned_date
  FROM store_returns sr
  JOIN date_dim d1
    ON d1.d_date_sk = sr.sr_returned_date_sk
   AND d1.d_date >= DATE '1999-01-01'
   AND d1.d_date <  DATE '2000-01-01'
  JOIN item i
    ON i.i_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
   AND i.i_category IN ('Home', 'Men', 'Music')
),
eligible_customers AS (
  SELECT
    c.c_customer_sk
  FROM customer c
  JOIN customer_address ca
    ON ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
  JOIN household_demographics hd
    ON hd.hd_demo_sk = c.c_current_hdemo_sk
  WHERE ca.ca_state IN ('MS', 'NC', 'NM', 'OK', 'TN')
    AND hd.hd_income_band_sk BETWEEN 14 AND 20
    AND hd.hd_buy_potential = '5001-10000'
)
SELECT
  min(c.c_customer_sk) AS min_c_customer_sk,
  min(ss.ss_item_sk) AS min_ss_item_sk,
  min(r.sr_ticket_number) AS min_sr_ticket_number,
  min(ws.ws_order_number) AS min_ws_order_number
FROM return_1999 r
JOIN store_sales ss
  ON ss.ss_item_sk = r.sr_item_sk
 AND ss.ss_ticket_number = r.sr_ticket_number
JOIN eligible_customers c
  ON c.c_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
JOIN web_sales ws
  ON ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND ws.ws_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON d2.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
 AND d2.d_date BETWEEN r.returned_date AND r.returned_date + interval '90' day
WHERE ss.ss_sales_price / ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 0.57 AND 0.77;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Introduce a return_1999 CTE that pre-filters store_returns by the 1999 return date (via date_dim d1) and by the item categories, so the driving fact-table input is reduced before joining store_sales and web_sales.

Introduce an eligible_customers CTE that pre-filters customer, customer_address (state list), and household_demographics (income band / buy potential) before joining to store_sales, avoiding the late application of the ca_state filter observed after the web_sales/date join in the original plan.

Replace implicit comma joins with explicit ANSI JOINs, placing selective predicates in the ON clauses. This makes the join graph clearer and allows the optimizer to evaluate the return-date item filter and customer demographics filter early.
Replace d1.d_year = 1999 with an equivalent sargable date range on d1.d_date (>= '1999-01-01' AND < '2000-01-01'), which can use an index on d_date and is easier for the planner to push down.
Fold the constants 57 * 0.01 and 77 * 0.01 into the literals 0.57 and 0.77 in the price-ratio predicate.

original_query: select min(c_customer_sk), min(ss_item_sk), min(sr_ticket_number), min(ws_order_number) FROM store_sales, store_returns, web_sales, date_dim d1, date_dim d2, item, customer, customer_address, household_demographics WHERE ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number AND ss_customer_sk = ws_bill_customer_sk AND ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk AND c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk AND c_current_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk AND ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk AND sr_item_sk = ws_item_sk AND i_item_sk = ss_item_sk AND i_category IN ('Jewelry', 'Music', 'Sports') AND sr_returned_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk AND ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk AND d2.d_date between d1.d_date AND (d1.d_date + interval '90' day) AND ca_state in ('IA', 'KS', 'MD', 'MO', 'OK') AND d1.d_year = 2000 AND hd_income_band_sk BETWEEN 14 AND 20 AND hd_buy_potential = '0-500' AND ss_sales_price / ss_list_price BETWEEN 38 * 0.01 AND 58 * 0.01 ;

WITH item_sub AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk
    FROM item
    WHERE i_category IN ('Jewelry', 'Music', 'Sports')
),
date_d1 AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk, d_date
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_year = 2000
),
date_d2 AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk, d_date
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_year IN (2000, 2001)
)
SELECT
    MIN(c.c_customer_sk),
    MIN(ss.ss_item_sk),
    MIN(sr.sr_ticket_number),
    MIN(ws.ws_order_number)
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN store_returns sr
    ON ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
   AND ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
JOIN web_sales ws
    ON ss.ss_customer_sk = ws.ws_bill_customer_sk
   AND ss.ss_item_sk = ws.ws_item_sk
JOIN date_d1 d1
    ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
JOIN date_d2 d2
    ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
JOIN item_sub i
    ON i.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
JOIN customer c
    ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
JOIN customer_address ca
    ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd
    ON c.c_current_hdemo_sk = hd.hd_demo_sk
WHERE d2.d_date BETWEEN d1.d_date AND d1.d_date + INTERVAL '90' DAY
  AND ca.ca_state IN ('IA', 'KS', 'MD', 'MO', 'OK')
  AND hd.hd_income_band_sk BETWEEN 14 AND 20
  AND hd.hd_buy_potential = '0-500'
  AND ss.ss_sales_price / ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 0.38 AND 0.58;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Simplify `38 * 0.01` and `58 * 0.01` to the literal constants `0.38` and `0.58` in the price-ratio predicate. This removes redundant runtime arithmetic and improves readability.

Add the safe derived predicate `d2.d_year IN (2000, 2001)` to date_dim d2. Since d1 is restricted to year 2000 and d2 must fall within 90 days of d1, any qualifying d2 row must be in 2000 or 2001; this prunes the d2 dimension early without changing semantics.

Replace implicit comma-style joins with explicit ANSI JOIN syntax and table aliases. This clarifies the join graph, keeps all join predicates explicit, and preserves the optimizer's ability to use existing indexes (store_sales_pkey, store_returns returned-date index, web_sales bitmap scans).

Introduce small, filter-only CTEs for the dimension tables (item by category, d1 by year 2000, d2 by years 2000/2001). These dimensions are small (item ~7k filtered rows, date_dim ~150/730 rows) so CTE materialization overhead is negligible, while large fact tables (store_sales 28.8M, store_returns 7.2M, web_sales 7.2M) are deliberately NOT wrapped in CTEs to avoid losing index-driven nested-loop join paths.

Rejected: creating a CTE over store_sales pre-filtered by the sales/list price ratio. This would force a full scan of a 28.8M-row fact table and lose the efficient store_sales_pkey lookup driven by (ss_item_sk, ss_ticket_number).

rewritten_query:
WITH eligible_dates AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_year = 2002
      AND d_moy BETWEEN 3 AND 6
),
eligible_items AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk
    FROM item
    WHERE i_category IN ('Electronics', 'Home', 'Women')
      AND i_manager_id BETWEEN 72 AND 81
),
store_eligible AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ss.ss_customer_sk
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN eligible_dates d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    JOIN eligible_items i ON i.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
    WHERE ss.ss_sales_price / ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 0.90 AND 1.00
),
web_eligible AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ws.ws_bill_customer_sk
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN eligible_dates d ON d.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
    JOIN eligible_items i ON i.i_item_sk = ws.ws_item_sk
    WHERE ws.ws_sales_price / ws.ws_list_price BETWEEN 0.90 AND 1.00
),
catalog_eligible AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT cs.cs_ship_customer_sk
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN eligible_dates d ON d.d_date_sk = cs.cs_sold_date_sk
    JOIN eligible_items i ON i.i_item_sk = cs.cs_item_sk
    WHERE cs.cs_sales_price / cs.cs_list_price BETWEEN 0.90 AND 1.00
)
SELECT
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt1,
    cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt2,
    cd.cd_credit_rating,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt3,
    cd.cd_dep_count,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt4,
    cd.cd_dep_employed_count,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt5,
    cd.cd_dep_college_count,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt6
FROM customer c
JOIN customer_address ca ON ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd ON cd.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
WHERE ca.ca_county IN ('Baldwin County','Cocke County','Elko County','Geauga County','Marengo County')
  AND c.c_birth_month IN (6, 7)
  AND cd.cd_marital_status IN ('U', 'S')
  AND cd.cd_education_status IN ('Advanced Degree', 'Primary')
  AND cd.cd_gender = 'F'
  AND c.c_customer_sk IN (SELECT ss_customer_sk FROM store_eligible)
  AND (c.c_customer_sk IN (SELECT ws_bill_customer_sk FROM web_eligible)
       OR c.c_customer_sk IN (SELECT cs_ship_customer_sk FROM catalog_eligible))
GROUP BY
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
    cd.cd_credit_rating,
    cd.cd_dep_count,

    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
    cd.cd_credit_rating,
    cd.cd_dep_count,
    cd.cd_dep_employed_count,
    cd.cd_dep_college_count
LIMIT 100;

Replaced the three correlated EXISTS subqueries on store_sales, web_sales, and catalog_sales with precomputed DISTINCT customer-key CTEs, eliminating repeated correlated index lookups and allowing hash semi-joins.

Created shared eligible_dates and eligible_items CTEs since the same date_dim (year 2002, months 3-6) and item (category, manager range) filters were repeated in all three EXISTS subqueries; the small dimension sets are now scanned/materialized once instead of three times.

Converted implicit comma joins to explicit ANSI INNER JOINs for customer / customer_address / customer_demographics, enabling the optimizer to choose hash joins instead of the original nested-loop pattern driven from the store_sales customer set.

original_query: select avg(ss_quantity) ,avg(ss_ext_sales_price) ,avg(ss_ext_wholesale_cost) ,sum(ss_ext_wholesale_cost) from store_sales    ,store    ,customer_demographics    ,household_demographics    ,customer_address    ,date_dim where s_store_sk = ss_store_sk and  ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and d_year = 2001 and((ss_hdemo_sk=hd_demo_sk and cd_demo_sk = ss_cdemo_sk and cd_marital_status = 'U' and cd_education_status = 'College' and ss_sales_price between 100.00 and 150.00 and hd_dep_count = 3    )or    (ss_hdemo_sk=hd_demo_sk and cd_demo_sk = ss_cdemo_sk and cd_marital_status = 'W' and cd_education_status = '2 yr Degree' and ss_sales_price between 50.00 and 100.00 and hd_dep_count = 1    ) or    (ss_hdemo_sk=hd_demo_sk and cd_demo_sk = ss_cdemo_sk and cd_marital_status = 'S' and cd_education_status = 'College' and ss_sales_price between 150.00 and 200.00 and hd_dep_count = 1    )) and((ss_addr_sk = ca_address_sk and ca_country = 'United States' and ca_state in ('IN', 'NM', 'VA') and ss_net_profit between 100 and 200    ) or    (ss_addr_sk = ca_address_sk and ca_country = 'United States' and ca_state in ('MT', 'OH', 'OR') and ss_net_profit between 150 and 300    ) or    (ss_addr_sk = ca_address_sk and ca_country = 'United States' and ca_state in ('GA', 'IL', 'TX') and ss_net_profit between 50 and 250    )) ;
rewritten_query:
WITH demo_patterns AS (
    SELECT * FROM (VALUES
        ('U', 'College',      100.00::numeric, 150.00::numeric, 3),
        ('W', '2 yr Degree',   50.00::numeric, 100.00::numeric, 1),
        ('S', 'College',      150.00::numeric, 200.00::numeric, 1)
    ) AS v(marital_status, education_status, min_sales_price, max_sales_price, dep_count)
),
addr_patterns AS (
    SELECT * FROM (VALUES
        ('IN', 100::numeric, 200::numeric),
        ('NM', 100::numeric, 200::numeric),
        ('VA', 100::numeric, 200::numeric),
        ('MT', 150::numeric, 300::numeric),
        ('OH', 150::numeric, 300::numeric),
        ('OR', 150::numeric, 300::numeric),
        ('GA',  50::numeric, 250::numeric),
        ('IL',  50::numeric, 250::numeric),
        ('TX',  50::numeric, 250::numeric)
    ) AS v(ca_state, min_net_profit, max_net_profit)
)
SELECT avg(ss.ss_quantity)            AS avg_quantity,
       avg(ss.ss_ext_sales_price)     AS avg_ext_sales_price,
       avg(ss.ss_ext_wholesale_cost)  AS avg_ext_wholesale_cost,
       sum(ss.ss_ext_wholesale_cost)  AS sum_ext_wholesale_cost
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN date_dim d
  ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
 AND d.d_year = 2001
JOIN store s
  ON s.s_store_sk = ss.ss_store_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON hd.hd_demo_sk = ss.ss_hdemo_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd
  ON cd.cd_demo_sk = ss.ss_cdemo_sk
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON ca.ca_address_sk = ss.ss_addr_sk
JOIN demo_patterns dp
  ON cd.cd_marital_status = dp.marital_status::character(1)
 AND cd.cd_education_status = dp.education_status::character(20)
 AND ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN dp.min_sales_price AND dp.max_sales_price
 AND hd.hd_dep_count = dp.dep_count
JOIN addr_patterns ap
  ON ca.ca_state = ap.ca_state::character(2)
 AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN ap.min_net_profit AND ap.max_net_profit
WHERE ca.ca_country = 'United States'
  AND ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 200.00
  AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Lift the common predicate ca_country = 'United States' out of the three address OR branches into a single WHERE predicate. Add necessary super-range pre-filters ss_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 200.00 and ss_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300, which are logically implied by the union of the OR sub-ranges and help filter store_sales earlier.

Replace the implicit comma joins with explicit ANSI JOIN clauses and move all join conditions (ss_hdemo_sk, ss_cdemo_sk, ss_addr_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_sold_date_sk) into the corresponding ON clauses. This clarifies the join graph and gives the optimizer a better structure for join reordering and predicate pushdown.

Replace the two complex OR predicate clusters with small pattern CTEs (demo_patterns and addr_patterns) joined to the fact table. The original semantics are (A1 OR A2 OR A3) AND (B1 OR B2 OR B3); joining independently to the two enumerating CTEs preserves this logic. Because the pattern rows are mutually exclusive (disjoint marital statuses and disjoint state groups), no row duplication is introduced. This avoids a 9-way UNION ALL that would rescan store_sales multiple times.

The date filter is expressed as a join condition on date_dim with d_year = 2001 directly in the ON clause, keeping the selective date-driven access path to store_sales (via ss_sold_date_sk) without materializing an additional CTE.

Explicitly fold the OR price ranges (100-150, 50-100, 150-200) into the covering range 50-200, and the OR net_profit ranges (100-200, 150-300, 50-250) into the covering range 50-300, using them as cheap early pre-filters on store_sales.

rewritten_query:
SELECT avg(ss.ss_quantity) AS avg_qty,
       avg(ss.ss_ext_sales_price) AS avg_sales_price,
       avg(ss.ss_ext_wholesale_cost) AS avg_wholesale_cost,
       sum(ss.ss_ext_wholesale_cost) AS sum_wholesale_cost
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
JOIN store s ON s.s_store_sk = ss.ss_store_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd ON hd.hd_demo_sk = ss.ss_hdemo_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd ON cd.cd_demo_sk = ss.ss_cdemo_sk
JOIN customer_address ca ON ca.ca_address_sk = ss.ss_addr_sk
WHERE d.d_year = 2001
  AND ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 200.00
  AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300
  AND hd.hd_dep_count IN (1, 3)
  AND cd.cd_marital_status = 'S'
  AND cd.cd_education_status IN ('Secondary', '2 yr Degree')
  AND ca.ca_country = 'United States'
  AND ca.ca_state IN ('MS','NY','VA','TN','TX','NC','NM','OK')
  AND (
       (cd.cd_education_status = 'Secondary' AND hd.hd_dep_count = 3
        AND ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 100.00 AND 150.00)
    OR (cd.cd_education_status = 'Secondary' AND hd.hd_dep_count = 1
        AND ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 100.00)
    OR (cd.cd_education_status = '2 yr Degree' AND hd.hd_dep_count = 1
        AND ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 150.00 AND 200.00)
  )
  AND (
       (ca.ca_state IN ('MS','NY','VA') AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 100 AND 200)
    OR (ca.ca_state IN ('MS','TN','TX') AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 150 AND 300)
    OR (ca.ca_state IN ('NC','NM','OK') AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 250)
  );

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Derived safe superset filters from the OR branches: ss_sales_price BETWEEN 50 AND 200, ss_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300, hd_dep_count IN (1,3), cd_marital_status='S', cd_education_status IN ('Secondary','2 yr Degree'), ca_country='United States', ca_state IN (8 states). These are implied by the original ORs and can be pushed early without changing results.

Converted implicit comma joins to explicit ANSI INNER JOINs, moving the join keys (ss_hdemo_sk=hd_demo_sk, ss_cdemo_sk=cd_demo_sk, ss_addr_sk=ca_address_sk) out of the OR branches into JOIN conditions. This reduces late join-filter evaluation and improves plan flexibility.

Moved dimension-level filters (hd_dep_count, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, ca_country, ca_state) out of the OR structure so the optimizer can filter dimension tables (household_demographics, customer_demographics, customer_address) before or during the join, instead of evaluating them as nested-loop join filters on every fact row.

Consolidated the overlapping numeric ranges across OR branches (sales price 50-100/100-150/150-200 → 50-200; net profit 50-250/100-200/150-300 → 50-300) into single bounding predicates, and simplified the duplicated hd_dep_count=1 conditions into hd_dep_count IN (1,3).

Considered a CTE to pre-filter store_sales but rejected it in the final rewrite: the CTE would be referenced only once, and on some PostgreSQL versions CTE materialization would add overhead on the 28.8M-row fact table. Direct joins with pushed-down predicates achieve the same effect with less risk.

rewritten_query:
WITH sales_2001 AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_quantity,
           ss.ss_ext_sales_price,
           ss.ss_ext_wholesale_cost,
           ss.ss_sales_price,
           ss.ss_net_profit,
           ss.ss_hdemo_sk,
           ss.ss_cdemo_sk,
           ss.ss_addr_sk,
           ss.ss_store_sk
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 200.00
      AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300
)
SELECT avg(ss.ss_quantity),
       avg(ss.ss_ext_sales_price),
       avg(ss.ss_ext_wholesale_cost),
       sum(ss.ss_ext_wholesale_cost)
FROM sales_2001 ss
JOIN store s ON s.s_store_sk = ss.ss_store_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd ON cd.cd_demo_sk = ss.ss_cdemo_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd ON hd.hd_demo_sk = ss.ss_hdemo_sk
JOIN customer_address ca ON ca.ca_address_sk = ss.ss_addr_sk
WHERE ca.ca_country = 'United States'
  AND (
        (hd.hd_dep_count = 3
         AND cd.cd_marital_status = 'U'
         AND cd.cd_education_status = 'College'
         AND ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 100.00 AND 150.00)
     OR
        (hd.hd_dep_count = 1
         AND (
               (cd.cd_marital_status = 'U'
                AND cd.cd_education_status = 'College'
                AND ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 100.00)
            OR
               (cd.cd_marital_status = 'S'
                AND cd.cd_education_status = 'Secondary'
                AND ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 150.00 AND 200.00)
         ))
  )
  AND (
        (ca.ca_state IN ('AR','OK') AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 100 AND 200)
     OR (ca.ca_state = 'TX'          AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 100 AND 300)
     OR (ca.ca_state = 'MN'          AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 150 AND 300)
     OR (ca.ca_state = 'KS'          AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300)
     OR (ca.ca_state IN ('MD','NV')  AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 250)
  );

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Hoist the common join predicates (ss_hdemo_sk=hd_demo_sk, cd_demo_sk=ss_cdemo_sk, ss_addr_sk=ca_address_sk, ca_country='United States') out of the OR blocks into explicit JOIN/WHERE clauses, and factor the repeated (cd_marital_status='U' AND cd_education_status='College') predicates into a single grouped OR.

Collapse the overlapping address OR branches into state-specific, disjoint net-profit ranges: AR/OK 100-200, TX 100-300 (union of 100-200 and 150-300), MN 150-300, KS 50-300 (union of 150-300 and 50-250), MD/NV 50-250. This removes overlapping OR evaluation and preserves the row-level OR semantics (each qualifying row counted once).

Replace comma-style joins with explicit ANSI INNER JOINs and a CTE (sales_2001) that pre-filters store_sales by d_year=2001 plus the enclosing ranges ss_sales_price BETWEEN 50 AND 200 and ss_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300, which are supersets of all OR branches and therefore equivalence-preserving.

FROM store_sales ss

JOIN date_dim d                ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
                              AND d.d_year = 2001
JOIN household_demographics hd ON hd.hd_demo_sk = ss.ss_hdemo_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd  ON cd.cd_demo_sk = ss.ss_cdemo_sk
JOIN customer_address ca       ON ca.ca_address_sk = ss.ss_addr_sk

  AND hd.hd_dep_count IN (1, 3)
  AND ca.ca_country = 'United States'
  AND ca.ca_state IN ('IN', 'NM', 'VA', 'MT', 'OH', 'OR', 'GA', 'IL', 'TX')

        (cd.cd_marital_status = 'U' AND cd.cd_education_status = 'College'

         AND hd.hd_dep_count = 3)
     OR (cd.cd_marital_status = 'W' AND cd.cd_education_status = '2 yr Degree'

WITH target_weeks AS (
    SELECT
        d_week_seq,
        CASE WHEN d_year = 1999 THEN 'this' ELSE 'last' END AS year_flag
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_year IN (1998, 1999)
      AND d_moy = 12
      AND d_dom = 5
),
store_triples AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        iss.i_brand_id,
        iss.i_class_id,
        iss.i_category_id
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN item iss ON ss.ss_item_sk = iss.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d1 ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
    WHERE d1.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND iss.i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Jewelry')
      AND iss.i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 37
      AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
),
catalog_triples AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        ics.i_brand_id,
        ics.i_class_id,
        ics.i_category_id
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN item ics ON cs.cs_item_sk = ics.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d2 ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
    WHERE d2.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND ics.i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Jewelry')
      AND ics.i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 37
      AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
),
web_triples AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        iws.i_brand_id,
        iws.i_class_id,
        iws.i_category_id
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN item iws ON ws.ws_item_sk = iws.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d3 ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk
    WHERE d3.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
),
cross_items AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        i.i_item_sk AS ss_item_sk,
        i.i_brand_id,
        i.i_class_id,
        i.i_category_id
    FROM item i
    JOIN store_triples s
      ON i.i_brand_id = s.i_brand_id
     AND i.i_class_id = s.i_class_id
     AND i.i_category_id = s.i_category_id
    JOIN catalog_triples c
      ON i.i_brand_id = c.i_brand_id
     AND i.i_class_id = c.i_class_id
     AND i.i_category_id = c.i_category_id
    JOIN web_triples w
      ON i.i_brand_id = w.i_brand_id
     AND i.i_class_id = w.i_class_id
     AND i.i_category_id = w.i_category_id
    WHERE i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 37
),
avg_sales AS (
    SELECT
        (COALESCE(s.total_sales, 0) + COALESCE(c.total_sales, 0) + COALESCE(w.total_sales, 0))
        / NULLIF(COALESCE(s.sales_count, 0) + COALESCE(c.sales_count, 0) + COALESCE(w.sales_count, 0), 0)
        AS average_sales
    FROM (
        SELECT SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) AS total_sales,
               COUNT(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) AS sales_count
        FROM store_sales ss
        JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100

    CROSS JOIN (
        SELECT SUM(cs.cs_quantity * cs.cs_list_price) AS total_sales,
               COUNT(cs.cs_quantity * cs.cs_list_price) AS sales_count
        FROM catalog_sales cs
        JOIN date_dim d ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
    ) c
    CROSS JOIN (
        SELECT SUM(ws.ws_quantity * ws.ws_list_price) AS total_sales,
               COUNT(ws.ws_quantity * ws.ws_list_price) AS sales_count
        FROM web_sales ws
        JOIN date_dim d ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100

),
store_sales_by_week AS (

)

rewritten_query:
WITH cross_items AS (
  SELECT i.i_item_sk AS ss_item_sk
  FROM item i
  JOIN (
    SELECT iss.i_brand_id AS brand_id,
           iss.i_class_id AS class_id,
           iss.i_category_id AS category_id
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN item iss ON ss.ss_item_sk = iss.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d1 ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
    WHERE d1.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND iss.i_category IN ('Books','Home','Sports')
      AND iss.i_manager_id BETWEEN 14 AND 23
      AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 78 AND 98
    INTERSECT
    SELECT ics.i_brand_id, ics.i_class_id, ics.i_category_id
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN item ics ON cs.cs_item_sk = ics.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d2 ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
    WHERE d2.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND ics.i_category IN ('Books','Home','Sports')
      AND ics.i_manager_id BETWEEN 14 AND 23
      AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 78 AND 98
    INTERSECT
    SELECT iws.i_brand_id, iws.i_class_id, iws.i_category_id
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN item iws ON ws.ws_item_sk = iws.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d3 ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk
    WHERE d3.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 78 AND 98
      AND iws.i_category IN ('Books','Home','Sports')
  ) x
    ON i.i_brand_id = x.brand_id
   AND i.i_class_id = x.class_id
   AND i.i_category_id = x.category_id
  WHERE i.i_category IN ('Books','Home','Sports')
    AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 14 AND 23
),
avg_sales AS (
  SELECT (COALESCE(ss_agg.sales,0) + COALESCE(cs_agg.sales,0) + COALESCE(ws_agg.sales,0))
         / NULLIF(ss_agg.cnt + cs_agg.cnt + ws_agg.cnt, 0) AS average_sales
  FROM (
    SELECT SUM(ss.ss_quantity*ss.ss_list_price) AS sales,
           COUNT(ss.ss_quantity*ss.ss_list_price) AS cnt
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 78 AND 98
  ) ss_agg
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT SUM(cs.cs_quantity*cs.cs_list_price) AS sales,
           COUNT(cs.cs_quantity*cs.cs_list_price) AS cnt
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN date_dim d ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 78 AND 98
  ) cs_agg
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT SUM(ws.ws_quantity*ws.ws_list_price) AS sales,
           COUNT(ws.ws_quantity*ws.ws_list_price) AS cnt
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN date_dim d ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 78 AND 98
  ) ws_agg
),
target_weeks AS (
  SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN d_year = 1999 AND d_moy = 12 AND d_dom = 13 THEN d_week_seq END) AS this_week,
         MAX(CASE WHEN d_year = 1998 AND d_moy = 12 AND d_dom = 13 THEN d_week_seq END) AS last_week
  FROM date_dim
  WHERE (d_year = 1999 AND d_moy = 12 AND d_dom = 13)
     OR (d_year = 1998 AND d_moy = 12 AND d_dom = 13)
),
store_summary AS (
  SELECT i.i_brand_id,
         i.i_class_id,
         i.i_category_id,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d.d_week_seq = tw.this_week THEN ss.ss_quantity*ss.ss_list_price END) AS ty_sales,
         COUNT(CASE WHEN d.d_week_seq = tw.this_week THEN 1 END) AS ty_number_sales,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d.d_week_seq = tw.last_week THEN ss.ss_quantity*ss.ss_list_price END) AS ly_sales,
         COUNT(CASE WHEN d.d_week_seq = tw.last_week THEN 1 END) AS ly_number_sales
  FROM store_sales ss
  JOIN item i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
  JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
  JOIN target_weeks tw ON d.d_week_seq IN (tw.this_week, tw.last_week)
  JOIN cross_items ci ON ci.ss_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
  WHERE i.i_category IN ('Books','Home','Sports')
    AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 14 AND 23
    AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 78 AND 98
  GROUP BY i.i_brand_id, i.i_class_id, i.i_category_id
)
SELECT 'store' AS ty_channel,
       s.i_brand_id AS ty_brand,
       s.i_class_id AS ty_class,
       s.i_category_id AS ty_category,
       s.ty_sales,
       s.ty_number_sales,
       'store' AS ly_channel,
       s.i_brand_id AS ly_brand,
       s.i_class_id AS ly_class,
       s.i_category_id AS ly_category,
       s.ly_sales,
       s.ly_number_sales
FROM store_summary s
CROSS JOIN avg_sales a
WHERE s.ty_sales > a.average_sales
  AND s.ly_sales > a.average_sales
ORDER BY ty_channel, ty_brand, ty_class, ty_category
LIMIT 100;

WITH candidate_items AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk,
           i_brand_id,
           i_class_id,
           i_category_id
    FROM item
    WHERE i_category IN ('Children','Men','Women')
      AND i_manager_id BETWEEN 49 AND 58
),
cross_items AS (
    SELECT ci.i_item_sk AS ss_item_sk,
           ci.i_brand_id,
           ci.i_class_id,
           ci.i_category_id
    FROM candidate_items ci
    JOIN (
        SELECT iss.i_brand_id AS brand_id,
               iss.i_class_id AS class_id,
               iss.i_category_id AS category_id
        FROM candidate_items iss
        JOIN store_sales ss ON ss.ss_item_sk = iss.i_item_sk
        JOIN date_dim d1 ON d1.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
        WHERE d1.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
        GROUP BY iss.i_brand_id, iss.i_class_id, iss.i_category_id
        INTERSECT
        SELECT ics.i_brand_id AS brand_id,
               ics.i_class_id AS class_id,
               ics.i_category_id AS category_id
        FROM candidate_items ics
        JOIN catalog_sales cs ON cs.cs_item_sk = ics.i_item_sk
        JOIN date_dim d2 ON d2.d_date_sk = cs.cs_sold_date_sk
        WHERE d2.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
        GROUP BY ics.i_brand_id, ics.i_class_id, ics.i_category_id
        INTERSECT
        SELECT iws.i_brand_id AS brand_id,
               iws.i_class_id AS class_id,
               iws.i_category_id AS category_id
        FROM item iws
        JOIN web_sales ws ON ws.ws_item_sk = iws.i_item_sk
        JOIN date_dim d3 ON d3.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
        WHERE d3.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
        GROUP BY iws.i_brand_id, iws.i_class_id, iws.i_category_id
    ) x
      ON x.brand_id = ci.i_brand_id
     AND x.class_id = ci.i_class_id
     AND x.category_id = ci.i_category_id
),
avg_sales AS (
    SELECT avg(x.quantity * x.list_price) AS average_sales
    FROM (
        SELECT ss.ss_quantity AS quantity,
               ss.ss_list_price AS list_price
        FROM store_sales ss
        JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
        UNION ALL
        SELECT cs.cs_quantity AS quantity,
               cs.cs_list_price AS list_price
        FROM catalog_sales cs
        JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = cs.cs_sold_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
        UNION ALL
        SELECT ws.ws_quantity AS quantity,
               ws.ws_list_price AS list_price
        FROM web_sales ws
        JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
    ) x
),
target_weeks AS (
    SELECT d_week_seq,
           d_year
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE (d_year = 1998 AND d_moy = 12 AND d_dom = 9)
       OR (d_year = 1999 AND d_moy = 12 AND d_dom = 9)
)
SELECT
    'store' AS ty_channel,
    c.i_brand_id AS ty_brand,
    c.i_class_id AS ty_class,
    c.i_category_id AS ty_category,
    SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) FILTER (WHERE w.d_year = 1999) AS ty_sales,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE w.d_year = 1999) AS ty_number_sales,
    'store' AS ly_channel,
    c.i_brand_id AS ly_brand,
    c.i_class_id AS ly_class,
    c.i_category_id AS ly_category,
    SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) FILTER (WHERE w.d_year = 1998) AS ly_sales,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE w.d_year = 1998) AS ly_number_sales
FROM cross_items c
JOIN store_sales ss ON ss.ss_item_sk = c.ss_item_sk
JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
JOIN target_weeks w ON w.d_week_seq = d.d_week_seq
CROSS JOIN avg_sales a
WHERE ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
GROUP BY c.i_brand_id, c.i_class_id, c.i_category_id
HAVING SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) FILTER (WHERE w.d_year = 1999) > MAX(a.average_sales)
   AND SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) FILTER (WHERE w.d_year = 1998) > MAX(a.average_sales)
ORDER BY ty_channel, ty_brand, ty_class, ty_category
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Pre-aggregate each channel branch (store_sales, catalog_sales, web_sales) with GROUP BY brand/class/category before the INTERSECT, so the set operation works on a few distinct dimension combinations instead of millions of duplicated fact rows, eliminating the huge sorts in the original plan.

Introduce candidate_items CTE that filters item by i_category IN ('Children','Men','Women') and i_manager_id BETWEEN 49 AND 58 once, and reuse it for the store/catalog branches, the outer cross_items join, and the final aggregation instead of repeating the same predicates. The web_sales branch is deliberately kept without the manager filter to preserve the original query's semantics.

Merge the two nearly identical this_year and last_year subqueries into a single scan of store_sales using conditional aggregation (SUM/COUNT ... FILTER (WHERE w.d_year = ...)) driven by a target_weeks CTE, halving the main fact-table access and join work.

Replace the IN subquery on cross_items with a direct join, and carry i_brand_id/i_class_id/i_category_id inside cross_items so the final query needs no extra join to item; cross_items is guaranteed distinct on item_sk, so the join cannot duplicate rows.

Fold date expressions: d_year between 1998 AND 1998+2 becomes BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000, d_year = 1998+1 becomes 1999, and the two scalar week-sequence subqueries are computed once in the target_weeks CTE. WITH sales_base AS (
    SELECT
        i.i_item_id,
        ca.ca_country,
        ca.ca_state,
        ca.ca_county,
        SUM(CAST(cs.cs_quantity    AS DECIMAL(12,2))) AS sum_qty,
        COUNT(cs.cs_quantity)                           AS cnt_qty,
        SUM(CAST(cs.cs_list_price  AS DECIMAL(12,2))) AS sum_list_price,
        COUNT(cs.cs_list_price)                         AS cnt_list_price,
        SUM(CAST(cs.cs_coupon_amt  AS DECIMAL(12,2))) AS sum_coupon_amt,
        COUNT(cs.cs_coupon_amt)                         AS cnt_coupon_amt,
        SUM(CAST(cs.cs_sales_price AS DECIMAL(12,2))) AS sum_sales_price,
        COUNT(cs.cs_sales_price)                        AS cnt_sales_price,
        SUM(CAST(cs.cs_net_profit   AS DECIMAL(12,2))) AS sum_net_profit,
        COUNT(cs.cs_net_profit)                         AS cnt_net_profit,
        SUM(CAST(c.c_birth_year     AS DECIMAL(12,2))) AS sum_birth_year,
        COUNT(c.c_birth_year)                           AS cnt_birth_year
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN date_dim d               ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN item i                   ON cs.cs_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN customer_demographics cd ON cs.cs_bill_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
    JOIN customer c               ON cs.cs_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    JOIN customer_address ca      ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND i.i_category = 'Jewelry'
      AND cd.cd_gender = 'F'
      AND cd.cd_education_status = 'College'
      AND c.c_birth_month = 5
      AND ca.ca_state IN ('MT', 'OH', 'OR')
      AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 84 AND 89
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id, ca.ca_country, ca.ca_state, ca.ca_county
)
SELECT
    i_item_id,
    ca_country,
    ca_state,
    ca_county,
    SUM(sum_qty)         / NULLIF(SUM(cnt_qty), 0)         AS agg1,
    SUM(sum_list_price)  / NULLIF(SUM(cnt_list_price), 0)  AS agg2,
    SUM(sum_coupon_amt)  / NULLIF(SUM(cnt_coupon_amt), 0)  AS agg3,
    SUM(sum_sales_price) / NULLIF(SUM(cnt_sales_price), 0) AS agg4,
    SUM(sum_net_profit)  / NULLIF(SUM(cnt_net_profit), 0)  AS agg5,
    SUM(sum_birth_year)  / NULLIF(SUM(cnt_birth_year), 0)  AS agg6
FROM sales_base
GROUP BY ROLLUP (i_item_id, ca_country, ca_state, ca_county)
ORDER BY ca_country, ca_state, ca_county, i_item_id
LIMIT 100;

original_query: select  i_brand_id brand_id, i_brand brand, i_manufact_id, i_manufact,  	sum(ss_ext_sales_price) ext_price   from date_dim, store_sales, item,customer,customer_address,store   where  d_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk     and ss_item_sk = i_item_sk     and ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk     and c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk     and ss_store_sk = s_store_sk     AND i_category  = 'Home'     and d_year=2002     and d_moy = 8     and substring(ca_zip,1,5) <> substring(s_zip,1,5)     and ca_state  = 'GA'     and c_birth_month = 4     and ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100  group by i_brand       ,i_brand_id       ,i_manufact_id       ,i_manufact  order by ext_price desc          ,i_brand          ,i_brand_id          ,i_manufact_id          ,i_manufact limit 100 ;

WITH sales AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_item_sk,
           ss.ss_customer_sk,
           ss.ss_store_sk,
           ss.ss_ext_sales_price
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2002
      AND d.d_moy = 8
      AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
),
item_home AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk, i_brand_id, i_brand, i_manufact_id, i_manufact
    FROM item
    WHERE i_category = 'Home'
),
customer_april AS (
    SELECT c_customer_sk, c_current_addr_sk
    FROM customer
    WHERE c_birth_month = 4
),
address_ga AS (
    SELECT ca_address_sk, substring(ca_zip, 1, 5) AS ca_zip5
    FROM customer_address
    WHERE ca_state = 'GA'
),
store_zip AS (
    SELECT s_store_sk, substring(s_zip, 1, 5) AS s_zip5
    FROM store
)
SELECT i.i_brand_id AS brand_id,
       i.i_brand AS brand,
       i.i_manufact_id,
       i.i_manufact,
       SUM(s.ss_ext_sales_price) AS ext_price
FROM sales s
JOIN item_home i ON i.i_item_sk = s.ss_item_sk
JOIN customer_april c ON c.c_customer_sk = s.ss_customer_sk
JOIN address_ga a ON a.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
JOIN store_zip st ON st.s_store_sk = s.ss_store_sk
                 AND st.s_zip5 <> a.ca_zip5
GROUP BY i.i_brand_id, i.i_brand, i.i_manufact_id, i.i_manufact
ORDER BY ext_price DESC,
         i.i_brand,
         i.i_brand_id,
         i.i_manufact_id,
         i.i_manufact

WITH frequent_ss_items AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.i_item_sk AS item_sk
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    JOIN item i ON i.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001

      AND i.i_category IN ('Books', 'Jewelry', 'Sports')

    HAVING count(*) > 4
),
max_store_sales AS (

    FROM (
        SELECT c.c_customer_sk, sum(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_sales_price) AS csales

        JOIN customer c ON c.c_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
        JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk

    ) customer_sales
),
best_ss_customer AS (
    SELECT c.c_customer_sk
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN customer c ON c.c_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
    WHERE c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1977 AND 1983
    GROUP BY c.c_customer_sk
    HAVING sum(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_sales_price) >

    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND d.d_moy = 10
      AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 2 AND 12
    UNION ALL
    SELECT ws.ws_quantity * ws.ws_list_price AS sales
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
    JOIN frequent_ss_items f ON f.item_sk = ws.ws_item_sk
    JOIN best_ss_customer b ON b.c_customer_sk = ws.ws_bill_customer_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND d.d_moy = 10
      AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 2 AND 12
) total_sales
LIMIT 100;

WITH date_2001 AS (
  SELECT d_date_sk
  FROM date_dim
  WHERE d_year = 2001
),
date_2001_07 AS (
  SELECT d_date_sk
  FROM date_dim
  WHERE d_year = 2001
    AND d_moy = 7
),
frequent_ss_items AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT item_sk
  FROM (
    SELECT ss.ss_item_sk AS item_sk
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_2001 d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    JOIN item i ON i.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
    WHERE i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 12 AND 31
      AND i.i_category IN ('Children', 'Home', 'Women')
    GROUP BY substring(i.i_item_desc, 1, 30),
             ss.ss_item_sk,
             ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    HAVING count(*) > 4
  ) f
),
max_store_sales AS (
  SELECT max(csales) AS tpcds_cmax
  FROM (
    SELECT c.c_customer_sk,
           sum(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_sales_price) AS csales
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_2001 d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    JOIN customer c ON c.c_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
    WHERE ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 30 AND 40
    GROUP BY c.c_customer_sk
  ) m
),
best_ss_customer AS (
  SELECT c.c_customer_sk
  FROM store_sales ss
  JOIN customer c ON c.c_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
  WHERE c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1940 AND 1946
  GROUP BY c.c_customer_sk
  HAVING sum(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_sales_price) >
         0.95 * (SELECT m.tpcds_cmax FROM max_store_sales m)
)
SELECT sum(sales) AS total_sales
FROM (

  JOIN date_2001_07 d ON d.d_date_sk = cs.cs_sold_date_sk
  JOIN frequent_ss_items f ON f.item_sk = cs.cs_item_sk
  JOIN best_ss_customer b ON b.c_customer_sk = cs.cs_bill_customer_sk
  WHERE cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 30 AND 40
  UNION ALL
  SELECT ws.ws_quantity * ws.ws_list_price AS sales
  FROM web_sales ws
  JOIN date_2001_07 d ON d.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
  JOIN frequent_ss_items f ON f.item_sk = ws.ws_item_sk
  JOIN best_ss_customer b ON b.c_customer_sk = ws.ws_bill_customer_sk
  WHERE ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 30 AND 40
) tmp2;

original_query: select   i_item_id  ,i_item_desc  ,s_store_id  ,s_store_name  ,sum(ss_net_profit) as store_sales_profit  ,sum(sr_net_loss) as store_returns_loss  ,sum(cs_net_profit) as catalog_sales_profit  from  store_sales  ,store_returns  ,catalog_sales  ,date_dim d1  ,date_dim d2  ,date_dim d3  ,store  ,item  where  d1.d_moy = 8  and d1.d_year = 2001  and d1.d_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk  and i_item_sk = ss_item_sk  and s_store_sk = ss_store_sk  and ss_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk  and ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk  and ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number  and sr_returned_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk  and d2.d_moy               between 8 and  8 + 2  and d2.d_year              = 2001  and sr_customer_sk = cs_bill_customer_sk  and sr_item_sk = cs_item_sk  and cs_sold_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk  and d3.d_moy               between 8 and  8 + 2  and d3.d_year              = 2001  group by  i_item_id  ,i_item_desc  ,s_store_id  ,s_store_name  order by  i_item_id  ,i_item_desc  ,s_store_id  ,s_store_name  limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH d1 AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_moy = 8
      AND d_year = 2001
),
d2_3 AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_moy BETWEEN 8 AND 10
      AND d_year = 2001
)
SELECT i.i_item_id,
       i.i_item_desc,
       s.s_store_id,
       s.s_store_name,
       SUM(ss.ss_net_profit) AS store_sales_profit,
       SUM(sr.sr_net_loss)   AS store_returns_loss,
       SUM(cs.cs_net_profit) AS catalog_sales_profit
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN d1 ON d1.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
JOIN store_returns sr
  ON sr.sr_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND sr.sr_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND sr.sr_ticket_number = ss.ss_ticket_number
JOIN d2_3 d2 ON d2.d_date_sk = sr.sr_returned_date_sk
JOIN catalog_sales cs
  ON cs.cs_bill_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
 AND cs.cs_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
JOIN d2_3 d3 ON d3.d_date_sk = cs.cs_sold_date_sk
JOIN store s ON s.s_store_sk = ss.ss_store_sk
JOIN item i ON i.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
GROUP BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
ORDER BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
LIMIT 100;
